title: Rollout safety checklist and SLO experiments notebook
body:
Purpose and quick context:
This doc is a working notebook for the next 30-day reliability-onboarding sprint focused on safe model rollouts and small-SLO experiments. Treat as living notes: hypotheses, quick checks, shallow-run experiments, and the minimum gating checklist required for canary traffic patterns. Not a final playbook — the goal is to converge to a minimal set of automatic gates and a runnable checklist that product teams can reuse.

Goals (30-day scope):
- Prove a repeatable canary flow that: accepts 5–10% traffic, runs for 3k requests or 6 hours (whichever first), and has automated pass/fail checks.
- Define 3 core SLOs for model-serving feature launches (latency, correctness/regression, availability) and an approach to measure quality drift during rollout.
- Build lightweight dashboards/alerts and a single-page runbook for on-call.

Primary hypotheses (we'll A/B test/validate):
H1: Traffic-weighted canaries with KV cache warming reduce p95 latency regressions compared to unweighted canaries.
H2: A combined quality metric (semantic-similarity drop + business-rule failures) detects model regressions within the first 500 requests.
H3: Auto-fallback to warm compatible-variant preserves availability with <1% extra token-cost when failures exceed threshold.

Stakeholders & owners (quick):
- Project lead: Avery Kim (eng-serving-runtime) — overall coordination
- Canary engineering owner: Mateo Alvarez — traffic config + telemetry hooks
- Quality + evals: Priya Rao — prompt set, similarity metric, threshold tuning
- Observability + alerts: Samira Chen — dashboards + runbook pages
- Product / Launch sponsor: Liam O'Connor — release gating decisions

Success metrics (to call a canary "pass"):
- Latency: p95 for canary <= baseline+p95_margin (baseline = previous stable model), margin default = 20%
- Errors: 5xx-equivalent rate <= baseline + 0.15% absolute (or < 0.5% total)
- Quality: similarity drop <= 0.03 (using embedding cosine on probe set) OR business-rule failures <= historical median + 2 sigma
- Availability: endpoint 99.5% during canary window
- Cost: token-per-inference increase <= +12% for candidate path (configurable)

Experiment matrix (short):
- Exp A: Weighted canary (10% traffic) with KV prefetch vs no prefetch; measure p95, p99, cold-start latency count.
- Exp B: Probe-set frequent sampling (every 50th request) to compute rolling similarity; compare detection time to larger-sample offline evals.
- Exp C: Auto-fallback enabled vs manual rollback (operator triggered); track customer impact and incident time-to-repair.

Minimum checklist before flipping traffic on:
- Telemetry hooks: request id, model_version, route, token_count, kv_cache_hits (added to prod logs).
- Dashboards: canary latency + error burn rate + quality probe stream visible in single pane.
- Alerts: p95 spike > margin for 5 minutes, error-rate increase > threshold for 3 minutes, similarity-drop alert on rolling window.
- Runbook stub published to Confluence + copy to on-call pinned messages.
- Postmortem template created and linked in the runbook.
- Canary config validated in staging and smoke-tested with synthetic load.

Operational details (notes / heuristics):
- Canary duration heuristics: min 1 hour, preferred 6 hours for user-facing features; minimum sample size 3k requests to get stable error rates for low-volume endpoints.
- Traffic ramp: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 30–90m windows if no alerts; backoff immediately on any alert.
- Cache-warming: run warmers at 0%->1% step; prefer synthetic warmers when probe set exists.
- Isolation: route canary via edge header (X-Canary-Version) and tag telemetry.

Gating & rollback triggers (auto):
- Immediate rollback if total 5xx > 0.5% absolute AND spike is sustained 3 sequential 1-minute buckets.
- Rollback if p95 > baseline + 40% for 10 minutes.
- Rollback on similarity-drop > 0.08 on rolling 500-probe window.
- Soft-fallback: if canary fails cheaply (latency spike but no quality regression), shift traffic to variant with lower-latency kernel.

Communication plan (during rollout):
- Slack channel: #rollouts (pinned message: canary id, owner, start time, dashboards URL).
- Standup updates: short note at +15m, +60m, +3h, end-of-window.
- If rollback happens: immediate incident bridge per standard SRE flow; pager to on-call if user-visible impact.

Quick dashboard wiring (what to show):
- Time-series: p50/p95/p99 latency for baseline and canary (same Y axis).
- Error-rate: 1m/5m windows, with absolute and relative deltas.
- Quality probe stream: recent probe responses, rolling similarity, and per-probe annotations (failed business-rule items).
- Cost delta: tokens-per-request moving average.

Risk register (brief, with mitigations):
- Risk: False positives in similarity metric => noisy rollbacks. Mitigation: require similarity alert + business-rule failures OR manual confirmation for first 3 rollouts.
- Risk: Canaries not representative of real user traffic => miss regressions. Mitigation: include stratified sampling by route and include rare-case probes.
- Risk: Telemetry cardinality explosion. Mitigation: sample logs; use aggregated metrics for retention beyond 1d.

Open questions / decisions to resolve in next 2 weeks:
- Decide default canary percent for low-volume endpoints (<10rps). Proposal: use event-count-based canary (3k requests) rather than percent.
- Choose semantic-similarity threshold standardization: 0.03 vs 0.05 baseline. Priya to run historical sweep on 6 last model rollouts.
- Cost-levers: agree to auto-disable fallback if token-cost increase > 20% (product decision).

Runbook quick links (to add into single-page runbook):
- Post-deploy checklist (smoke-tests, probes): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RI/Canary+smoke+recipes
- Emergency rollback steps (CLI + Console): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RI/Rollback+Runbook
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/serving/canary-overview
- Pager on-call rota: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RI/Oncall+Shifts

Mini-retrospective template (to fill after each canary):
- What happened (timeline):
- Why it happened (root cause hypothesis):
- What we learned / changed:
- Action items (owner + ETA):

Next actions (this week):
- Mateo: wire kv_cache and request_id into prod logs (due 2026-01-22).
- Priya: run similarity historical sweep and propose thresholds (due 2026-01-25).
- Samira: dashboard fast-path and alert ruleset v0 (due 2026-01-27).
- Avery: draft single-page runbook and link to Confluence (due 2026-01-29).

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider a simple "health score" composite metric combining normalized latency/error/quality with tunable weights — use as quick binary gate for low-signal endpoints.
- Investigate cheap canary-only local caches to reduce cold-start noise.
- Explore model checkpoint diffing (schema + tokenizer changes) as pre-rollout sanity check.

Appendix: quick templates
- Canary start message (copy-paste):
  START-CANARY {canary-id} | owner: @AveryKim | model: vX.Y | percent: 10% | start: 2026-01-xxTxx:xxZ | dash: <grafana link>

- Rollback message template (copy-paste):
  ROLLBACK {canary-id} | triggered-by: <alert/manual> | cause: <short> | immediate action: traffic->stable, open bridge, notify product

This notebook will be iterated on as we run the first three canaries. Keep notes here rather than scattering in Slack; we'll extract a final one-page canonical checklist once items stabilize.

-- Avery
